text:
sam: snyk-bot just flagged a HIGH vuln in the base image we use for service-graph. saw it in CI image-scan job.

snyk-bot: Vulnerability detected: CVE-2025-3389 in libcrypto (base-image: redwood/base:2024-11). Severity: HIGH. Fix available in 1.2.4. Reference: https://vuln.example/CVE-2025-3389

tess: ugh. that base is shared across ~8 services. which images are affected?

sam: service-graph, event-processor, realtime-ingest — CI matrix shows failures for those three. I pasted the scan output from CI below:

```
Scan: docker.io/redwood/base:2024-11
Component: libcrypto 1.2.3 -> CVE-2025-3389 (HIGH)
Paths: /usr/lib/libcrypto.so
Fix: upgrade to libcrypto 1.2.4 or use base image redwood/base:2025-01
```

alejandro: can we do an emergency rebuild of the base image with libcrypto patched and push to the registry? we should also regenerate SBOMs.

pritam: agreed. action items: 1) rebuild base with patched libcrypto 2) trigger dependent image rebuilds (CI pipeline) 3) publish SBOMs + link in release notes 4) create short rollback plan if something breaks.

sam: +1. also want to add a temporary policy: block the old base tag in our runtime deploy gate until rebuilt images pass smoke tests.

tess: who can approve the rebuild + promote? I think we should limit approvals to infra leads (RBAC) and log approvals in audit.

alejandro: I'll take the rebuild. will tag redwood/base:2025-02-hotfix and sign the image. we should use cosign with KMS signing key. do we need to rotate keys after this?

pritam: No immediate KMS rotation required unless key was compromised. But we MUST record the signing event in the audit log and add the SBOM entry with build metadata (git sha, builder image, patch note).

sam: created a short incident: incident-bot created INC-2026-014 (supply-chain image vuln). tagging @security-oncall.

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-014 created. Severity: S2. Communication channel: #eng-security.

alejandro: rebuilding now. ETA ~20m for base image build + SBOM generation. I'll push intermediate manifests to internal registry: registry.redwood/internal/base:2025-02-hotfix-draft

tess: once pushed, trigger CI rebuilds for dependents and add a canary rollout to dedicated to verify. Log all promotion events to audit-log S3 path: s3://redwood-audit/image-promotions/2025-02-14/INC-2026-014.txt

sam: quick checklist for post-containment: - update inventory (SBOM) - notify customers on affected dedicated/private deployments? - update runbooks to include this CVE mapping

pritam: for customer comms we should coordinate with product. I'll open a ticket in #support to draft a short note. keep wording: "we patched a third-party library in base images; we rebuilt and validated images; no evidence of exploit"

alejandro: base image pushed and signed. cosign signature: cosign:sha256:abcd... SBOM at registry blob  sha256:ef12... Linking in the incident ticket.

tess: CI triggered, dependent builds green for service-graph and event-processor, realtime-ingest has a flaky test failing — investigating. will hold main rollout for realtime-ingest until green.

sam: good. I've blocked old tag in deploy-gate and added an exception for the hotfix tag until full rollout completes. audit entries should show who did the block and when.

pritam: follow-ups: - add CI step to auto-scan new base image tags and auto-generate SBOMs, - add RBAC rule so only infra leads can promote base images to 'stable', - ensure KMS signing events are forwarded to our SIEM for correlation.

alejandro: noted. I'll create PRs for CI and RBAC rules.

sam: closing loop — update this thread when realtime-ingest is green and canary passes. then we'll schedule a short postmortem to capture timeline and any tooling gaps. :thumbsup:

pritam: will write a brief post-incident note and add remediation tickets.

incident-bot: INC-2026-014 status updated: containment achieved.

sam: thanks all.
